sentences.text: Xuan did his first one at thirteen and said the name of a friend, which he now describes as the correct answer to a question he had not understood.
He did his second at fourteen and said his grandmother, who was ill.

He had thought about that one for six weeks and had gone into the water knowing exactly what he was going to say, and he has since decided that this was the mistake — that a name you have carried around for six weeks is a name you have already used up.
What he remembers is not the saying.

What he remembers is that the water was very cold and that a fish went past him about a metre away, going up, hardly moving, with its back out and the light on it, and that it was much bigger than he had understood salmon to be.
She died in the October, and in the following June — and this is the part he has never fully explained to himself — he did not go to the river at all.
He stayed at the house and helped with a gate that did not need fixing, and his father did not say a word about it either that day or since.
At fifteen he went to the source instead.
The Sella rises in the Fuente del Infierno, in the mountains, and it is about forty kilometres by the road and rather less if you are willing to be uncomfortable.
Xuan was willing.

He told his mother he was going walking with two friends, which was two-thirds a lie, and he went up on the bus to Cangas and walked from there and slept out one night in a way that he does not recommend.
What he expected — and he is prepared to be laughed at for this — was something.
Not a marker.
He was fifteen and not stupid.
But he thought there might be a place.
A pool that people had visited.
A cairn.

Something with the shape of an ending on it, because a thing that has been going for four hundred years and that delivers something to a specific location ought to have worn a mark into that location.
The Fuente del Infierno comes out of a cliff.
It is a good spring and it is a great deal of water and it makes an enormous noise, and there is wet rock and beech and a smell of cold stone, and there is nothing there.
No cairn.
No path except the ordinary one.
No names cut into anything.
Nothing anybody has left, ever, apart from a Fanta can that Xuan carried out with him for forty kilometres out of a feeling he could not have named.
He sat on a rock for most of an afternoon.
He had walked forty kilometres for it.
He had slept in a bus shelter above Cangas with his coat over his legs.
He was fifteen and extremely tired and there was a great deal of cold water coming out of a cliff and making a noise, and he sat there and waited to feel something, and what he felt was hungry.
And no salmon can get up there.
That is the thing that finished it.

He had known it before he set out and had somehow managed not to think about it: there are four weirs and a fall between Ribadesella and Cangas alone, and above Cangas the river becomes something no fish has ever gone up.
The salmon spawn in the middle reaches, in the gravel, in November, and they die there, and they have never once been anywhere near the Fuente del Infierno in the whole history of either species.
